newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium says not alone in problem over derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Belgium says not alone in problem over derivatives.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Tuesday a number of European countries had problems in valuing debt management operations involving derivatives in their national accounts.
"The same problems exist in other neighbouring countries...because European accounting rules do not allow us to value (the operations)," he told a Belgian parliamentary committee.
The committee was questioning Maystadt for the second time in two weeks over secretive, botched foreign exchange contracts that could cost Belgium more than 33 billion francs.
While under Maystadt's authority, the Treasury has admitted it set up a number of foreign exchange swap and options positions that, if closed now, would cost 32.6 billion francs.
If the contracts were left to mature, the cost would be 33.5 billion, based on today's exchange and interest rates, .

In addition, 5.3 billion francs have already been lost on the operations, carried out between June 1992 and October 1993 and straddling the crises in Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) in September 1992 and July 1993.
Opposition criticism of the contracts has centred on responsibility for the decisions and on when Belgium's public accounts office was informed of the transactions.
Opposition party members have also questioned whether the Treasury operated some kind of off-balance sheet "black account" to cover part of its losses or shift them to the national debt.
